text:
Samira Alvarez: Quick RFC follow-up — proposal to add a short affinity debounce window to reduce flapping when tenants move between active regions. thinking 20-60s. thoughts?
Kevin Park: Can you sketch the failure modes we're trying to avoid?
Samira Alvarez: Two cases: 1) transient network blips cause rapid residency churn and hot K/V cache misses, 2) quick autoscale shifts that move leases between regions and cause duplicate warmups. want a small hysteresis so we don't immediately evict.
Nate Li: Numbers matter. If debounce=30s and eviction_grace=300s, we'd reduce duplicate model loads by ~40% in our sims. but increases chance of serving from a non-preferred region for short period.
Olivia Chen: Data residency / compliance concern — serving from non-resident region for 30s might violate some residency contracts. need a whitelist/opt-out per-tenant.
Samira Alvarez: Agreed — default debounce should be opt-in for residency-sensitive tenants. propose tenant config flag "allow_transient_cross_region_serving".
Cheng Wu: KV cache impact: our LRU fill rate depends on stable owner for ~5min. if we debounce short moves we keep cache entries alive and avoid cold-starts. downside: split-brain risk during longer partition.
Kevin Park: How do we detect partition vs small blip? We already have heartbeat+lease TTL. Maybe tie debounce to consecutive failed heartbeats threshold rather than wall-clock only?
Nate Li: Implementation sketch: debounce window + handshake epoch check. Pseudocode:
```
if new_region_request && !tenant.residency_protected:
  if last_lease_change_ts + debounce_window > now:
    prefer current_owner until handshake confirms
  else:
    perform takeover
```
Also add metric: residency_debounce_applied{tenant,region}=1
```
Kevin Park: That looks reasonable. how does takeover handshake work with in-flight requests?
Samira Alvarez: plan: short-circuit new connection routing to current owner; new owner queues takeover and pulls KV snapshot; once snapshot complete it flips. existing requests continue until TTL.
Olivia Chen: For legal teams: need audit trail (who served which token and from which region). That means per-request region tag and a residency_change event in audit log.
Maria Gomez: SLO question: if we prefer owner for debounce window, latency SLO might spike for users far from owner. We need a per-tenant latency-cost tradeoff knob in the console.
Cheng Wu: Also consider adding a safety cutoff: if handshake doesn't complete within X seconds, force local serve with a warning and increment a "forced_local_due_to_handshake_timeout" metric.
Samira Alvarez: Good call. Suggested defaults: debounce_window=30s, eviction_grace=300s, handshake_timeout=45s. residency_opt_out=true for regulated tenants.
Kevin Park: Can we ship this behind a feature flag and enable for 10% of non-regulated tenants? rollout plan?
Nate Li: Yep — feature flag + Canary on Dedicated clusters. We'll enable rollout-monitoring dashboard for cache-hit, latency, residency_debounce_applied, handshake_durations.
InfraBot: Deploy-bot: canary rollout staged (infra/canary) started at 2025-07-10T14:03Z — job id deploy-5832.
Olivia Chen: Add legal + infosec to the rollout announcement. they'll want the opt-out knob and audit schema before GA.
Maria Gomez: Also add an alert if handshake_timeout rate > 5% in a 5m window.
Samira Alvarez: OK assigning action items: Nate -> impl debounce + metrics PR; Cheng -> KV snapshot optimization for takeover; Kevin -> rollout plan and dashboards; Olivia -> coordinate with legal for opt-out wording; Maria -> SLO alert thresholds. I'll open RFC follow-up with configs and default values. :thumbsup:
